title: Autism and Parenting Strategies
learningGoal: Support parents to understand autism, reduce sensory overload, and use strengths-based parenting strategies.
microLesson: Autistic children often experience the world differently. They may have sensory sensitivities, communication differences, or strong interests. Behaviour is often a form of communication, not defiance. Parents can support autistic children by reducing sensory triggers, using visual supports, offering predictable routines, and celebrating strengths. A calm, patient, and structured approach helps children feel safe and understood.
activity: Identify one sensory trigger your child experiences (noise, lights, textures). Make one small adjustment and reflect on how it affected your child.
